adjudication_label: Oxidation Stability and Oxide Phase Formation
canonical_question: Why were oxidation tests conducted at exactly 1000 °C and 1300 °C for the MoNbTaTiW RHEA with Si-20Cr-20Fe coating, and is 1300 °C near the melting point or phase instability limit of the silicide layer?

The evidence does not contain the necessary mechanism to bridge this specific temperature gap in the context of the specific Cr2O3 interaction.

question_variants.question: Why were oxidation tests conducted at exactly 1000 °C and 1300 °C, and is 1300 °C near the melting point or phase instability limit of the silicide layer?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The oxidation tests were conducted at exactly 1000 °C and 1300 °C to study the evolution of the coating structure. The provided text does not specify if 1300 °C is near the melting point or phase instability limit of the silicide layer, nor does it explain the selection criteria for these specific temperatures beyond the study of structural evolution.

answers.answer: The oxidation temperature was set to 1000 °C and 1300 °C to show the anti-oxidation mechanism of the silicide coating by studying the evolution of the structure and compositions. The text does not confirm if 1300 °C is near the melting point or phase instability limit.
answers.measurement_outcome: Structure evolution studied at these temperatures.
answers.boundary_limitation: No mention of melting points or phase instability limits in the abstract.
evidence_spans: The aim of this paper is to explore the feasibility of the Si-20Cr-20Fe coating in improving the oxidation resistance of MoNbTaTiW RHEA. The Si-20Cr-20Fe coating was prepared on the surface of MoNbTaTiW RHEA by a fused slurry method. To show the anti-oxidation mechanism of the silicide coating, the evolution of the structure and compositions of the coating at 1000 °C and 1300 °C were studied.
